title: Reading model output
lead: Should your app wait for the whole answer, show it as it arrives, or read it as data?

sections.title: Read the complete response
sections.body:
With a regular response, your application waits for generation to finish before reading the result. This works well for scripts and background jobs.
The response may also include usage and finish information, so check its structure before extracting the text.

sections.title: Streaming output
sections.body:
Streaming sends incremental events or fragments so an interface can show content sooner. It improves time to first content, but does not guarantee a faster overall task.
Network chunks are not complete messages. Parse the service or SDK event protocol and handle errors, interruptions, and completion. Do not JSON.parse each raw network chunk.

sections.title: Structured output
sections.body:
Suppose you want to save an itinerary to a database. You need a destination, a trip length, and daily plans. Asking for named fields is easier to work with than extracting them from prose.
Use the API’s structured output features when available, then validate the result in your code. Asking for JSON does not by itself guarantee valid syntax, the right fields, or accurate content.

sections.title: Choose what fits the task
sections.body:
Explanations read by a user can stream; classification results consumed by code suit structured output.
Structured responses can also be streamed, but incomplete fragments should not be treated as complete business objects.

note: If an action depends on an approved field, validate its boolean type and business authorization instead of searching the answer for “approved.”
